title: How Light Helps Plants Make Food
subject: Science

metadata.objective: Explain that light provides energy plants use to make food and use evidence to distinguish a lit leaf from a covered leaf.

paragraphs: Leaves are often positioned where they can receive light. Light is not the plant's food; it supplies the energy the leaf uses to make food from raw materials.

content.label: Do not confuse raw materials with food
content.body: Soil supplies water and minerals. The plant makes its food rather than taking ready-made food from the soil.

items.text: The plant makes food from raw materials.

content.caption: Inputs and energy involved when a leaf makes food.
content.alt_text: A planned diagram showing sunlight reaching a leaf, water entering from the roots, carbon dioxide entering the leaf, and food being made.

content.caption: A controlled comparison of lit and covered leaf areas.

content.title: Reasoning from the evidence
content.problem: A leaf is partly covered while the rest remains in light. Food-making evidence is later found only in the uncovered part. What conclusion is supported?

steps.text: Identify what changed: access to light.
Check that both parts belong to the same leaf and share other conditions.
Compare the result: evidence appears in the lit part but not the covered part.
Connect the changed condition to the different result.

content.answer: The comparison supports the conclusion that light is required for the leaf to make food.
content.check: The conclusion should name light and use the difference between covered and uncovered parts.

content.instructions: Answer in one or two complete sentences.

items.prompt: Explain why covering part of a leaf helps show that light is needed for the plant to make food.

content.stem: Which statement best describes the role of soil in plant food making?

options.text: Soil is the food the plant eats.
Soil supplies water and minerals, but the plant makes food in its leaves.
Soil supplies sunlight to the roots.

entries.answer: The covered part does not receive light while the uncovered part does. When food-making evidence appears only in the lit part, the changed condition shows that light is required.
alternatives: A correct answer compares covered and uncovered parts and links the different result to light.
entries.rubric: 2 marks: identifies light as the changed condition and connects the different result to food making. 1 mark: states light is needed without using the comparison.
